proposition: According to Melvin-Koushki, Dānishpazhūh called Ibn Turka the 'Spinoza of Iran' as a rhetorical call to edit his works, and Zarrīnkūb objected that the title misrepresents his more mystical and lettrist concerns.

mediation.who: Muḥammad Taqī Dānishpazhūh; ʿAbd al-Ḥusayn Zarrīnkūb
mediation.note: The position is this scholar's own; we have it only as summarised by Melvin-Koushki.
MK argues a rival reading (Ibn Turka as occult philosopher) and in places calls this reading an error; his summary may compress or foreshorten it.
